checks: One shared orthogonal frame preserves both positive axis arrows, the horizontal extension left of the origin and well past the last trace endpoint, and the vertical extension below the baseline and above both full maxima.
Source and both complete edition texts reconcile the voltage glyph as u_p; rendered u-subscript-p, O and t are correctly placed, clear, and no extra tick/calibration labels appear.
Exactly three rising segments, two full vertical resets and three rising-run baseline crossings. The third run ends below the full maxima: no invented fourth rising cycle or third reset.
The trace begins below the origin at the negative floor, rather than beginning at zero. Solid segments join continuously and preserve both equal completed rises.
Straight axes, equalized completed slopes/heights and vertical resets are explicitly declared modern regularization, not measured source time/voltage facts.
At actual 640px media width all three SVG text labels have font-size 22px, exceeding the 16px minimum; the existing render reports no collisions.

The full-width image shows all labels and geometry with clear margins. At the 331px mobile scroll end the final partial run, t and right arrow are visible; metadata binds the unchanged SVG and records scrollLeft 309 = 640 - 331.
No Cyrillic/Chinese cultural wording, Soviet symbols, numeric calibration, answers, or answer-bearing annotations are visible.

apparatus: Complete upright dark housing and substantial lower casing band, light four-corner mounting plate, actual round CRT, double rim, and all four fasteners remain visible in the full-width preview.

Circularizing scan distortion, straightening casing edges and making the fastener holes clear are declared schematic regularization. There are no invented knobs, ports, status lights, rectangular display or added calibrated axes.

finiteGraticule.interpretation: The 12x12 assertion is a genuine finite rectangular subset, with 13 vertical and 13 horizontal core tracks and all four corners inside the screen; it is not falsely labelled as the whole circular lattice. The remaining six vertical and four horizontal whole tracks, and both extensions of each core track, form the complete independently counted source lattice.
finiteGraticule.offsetAndRegularization: The source mid-track positions are close to, but not exactly at, the scanned round-screen center; tracks lean with scan skew. The candidate explicitly straightens/equal-spaces them in one phase centered at user coordinates [320,394], not at the global canvas origin. This center-phase normalization is modern regularization, not an exact source-coordinate or calibration claim. The narrower horizontal family and all boundary fragments are retained.
finiteGraticule.actualSvgEvidence: Parsed existing SVG line elements, grouped and joined collinear intervals, and derived 19/17 distinct tracks. No gaps or extra tracks; complete chord endpoints match the radius-212 screen boundary to a maximum 0.0000004791px coordinate error.
finiteGraticule.assertionCoverage: All 62 non-core segment pieces map to matching displacement assertions; 72 pointOnCircle assertions cover both ends of all 36 complete tracks. The source graticule group maps the gridDimensions assertion and these extent assertions. No objectCount substitutes for grid dimensions.
finiteGraticule.boundaryFragments: Short left/right vertical tracks and top/bottom horizontal chords are visible; round rim fragments are not counted as additional horizontal tracks.

checks: One continuous solid path descends first, then alternates through decreasing excursions. All four peaks, all four troughs and the final short falling tail are present.
The source-bound landmark order and positions relative to the graticule remain recognizable. Smooth monotone cubic interpolation is disclosed regularization, not a fitted analytic sine or decay law.

All ten candidate endpoints/extrema are matched to the nine mapped displacement assertions and the existing SVG path exactly. Monotone cubic pieces introduce no extra interior extrema or extra terminal cycle.
The last endpoint is inside the round screen; there is no constant-amplitude replacement, dashed envelope, flat extended tail, numerical voltage/time scale or added labelled zero axis.

Visible curve plus half of its 4px stroke is certified inside the radius-212 screen: curve radius upper bound 209.0127864px, including between-sample derivative bounds. Some invisible control handles lie outside the circle; they are not visible geometry and do not cause clipping.

display: Instructional fixed 640px media is preserved in both previews; the graticule and solid trace remain distinct in the CSS-resolved full-width image, with no blank/black failed raster.

At the 331px mobile scroll end, the final oscillations and falling tail, right rim, right mounting corner regions and fasteners are visible. Metadata records scrollLeft 309 = 640 - 331 and binds the unchanged SVG.
There are no visible text labels in source or candidate, so the 16px text minimum is not applicable rather than an invented text-size measurement.
Mobile's left-side viewport crop is intentional horizontal scrolling, not deleted apparatus or clipped SVG geometry; complete source coverage was inspected in the full-width image.
fig-25.cultureAndAnswerLeak: pass: no source cultural glyphs, symbols, archival texture, numeric calibration, labels revealing a task answer, or extra apparatus wording.

inventoryReconciliation.note: The first independent visual estimate put the fig-25 trace start near source y=211. Later read-only scanline analysis distinguishes the ordinary x=72..75 graticule stroke at y=205/209/213 from the widening curve near y=225/229. Thus that early y=211 estimate was a grid/trace merger, not a reliable curve endpoint fact. Candidate start around source [72,226] is compatible with the actual merged trace start. The frozen inventory is retained unchanged as FIRST evidence; this explicit clarification is not an author-spec-derived replacement inventory.
inventoryReconciliation.sourceCoordinatePrecision: Other source landmark coordinates in the independent inventory are approximate pixel observations, not calibrated graph values. The two editions ask for the sweep and decaying oscillation mechanism, not numerical readings.
